pregame.whyWatch: Division game: Broncos 2-2, 3rd in the AFC West; Chargers 0-4, 4th in the AFC West.
pregame.pressurePoint: Broncos passing-down offense vs Chargers passing-down defense. The Broncos are No. 13 of 32 in passing-downs success (40%). The Chargers rank No. 28 on passing downs (45%). A clear edge, the kind that shapes a game plan. The Broncos convert the long downs the Chargers need to win. A third-and-8 is not a stop here. Watch the Broncos on third-and-long. Two conversions in the first half break the Chargers plan.

The Chargers are No. 11 of 32 in rush success rate (45%) and No. 23 in EPA a carry (-0.13). The Broncos rank No. 18 against the run (42%) and No. 31 by EPA a carry (0.08). A real edge, not a lock. The Chargers should stay on schedule on the ground, which keeps third downs short and the clock moving.

The Chargers are No. 8 of 32 in pass explosiveness (1.40) and No. 30 in pass success rate (38%). The Broncos rank No. 15 at limiting explosive passes (1.30) and No. 14 in pass success allowed (45%). A real edge, not a lock. The Chargers have the deep ball available. Watch whether the Broncos roll a safety over after the first one.

The Broncos are No. 24 in pass explosiveness (1.23) and No. 24 in pass success rate (42%), and the Chargers are No. 27 at limiting explosive passes (1.39) and No. 23 in pass success allowed (48%). Strength on strength. The Broncos take shots and the Chargers give up few. Whoever wins the first deep ball changes the other side's call sheet.
